current_bottleneck: The 510a frontier is risk-manager presentable but still misses lower stress/regime inclusion. 560a implemented the synthetic-prior pretraining scaffold, but the tiny smoke checkpoint is not a candidate model and scored only 1/11 because it was deliberately undertrained and low-capacity.
last_result_summary: 560a added a deterministic synthetic IV-surface prior generator and a 340c-compatible synthetic pretraining script. Focused tests passed (4 passed). A small 512-window, 2-epoch synthetic pretrain reduced validation loss from 0.9385 to 0.8483, adapted successfully on 128 real windows, and ran through the 11-suite smoke path, scoring 1/11. This validates plumbing, not model quality.
next_step_recommendation: Run a scaled 561a TimePFN-style experiment with 340c/392a-sized capacity, thousands of synthetic windows, full 441-window real adaptation, and official validation if runtime permits. Judge whether stress/regime lower inclusion improves without sacrificing conditionality, dependence, mean reversion, and path realism.
current_best_note: 510a remains the best current risk prototype: 8/11 and risk-readiness 3/4, failing only lower-only regime inclusion under risk framing. 555a ties 8/11 but is not better; 558a is below frontier.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
